title: Pair in a sorted price list
description:
You solved the budget pair problem in week 2 with a dictionary. This time the price list is already **sorted ascending**, which lets you do it with no extra memory.

Write `sorted_pair(prices, budget)` that returns indices `[i, j]` with `i < j` such that `prices[i] + prices[j] == budget`, or `[]` if there is no such pair. The tests have at most one valid pair.

**Example**

```
sorted_pair([10, 25, 40, 60, 90], 100)
# [0, 4]
```
hints: Start with one index at the smallest price and one at the largest.
If the sum is too small, the only way to grow it is to move the left index right. If it is too big, move the right index left.
